summary: Spider-Bot S 1.0, phase 3 simplify: N10 -> pinion 14 T -> transfer 17/13 T -> idler 2 -> 4 cranks (10 T, m 1.0) via 3 idlers; drive unit split into 3 flat screwed parts (journal-cap, motor-u, transfer-cheek), no sleeves, M3 only; grams = solid volume x 1.24 (100 % infill), from the S 1.0 STLs and boxes

parts.name: base
parts.role: ground: bowl with 8 open-top leg windows, keel bosses, front snap ribs, back-sheet pocket (phase 2, unchanged)

parts.name: body
parts.role: shell snapped on the base, eye bores, switch window (unchanged)
parts.why_separate: the visible shell, lifts off for service

parts.name: legs
parts.role: 8 legs from cad/legs on the crank pins (unchanged)
parts.why_separate: each leg swings on its own pin

parts.name: spine
parts.role: two 2.0 walls with 4 open-top journal slots, keel; idler holes: -x wall M3 pilot, +x wall STEEL (no thread, walls not squeezed)
parts.why_separate: ground of the gear train, screwed to the base keel

parts.name: crankshafts
parts.role: 4 cranks, 10 T m 1.0, journals Ø4.3, Ø3 pins (unchanged)
parts.print_orient: the current orientation (phase 3 local work: support 137 mm² each)

parts.name: idlers
parts.role: 3 idlers 10 T, bore Ø3.3 on their M3 shank (B: no sleeves)
parts.why_separate: each turns on its own axle

parts.name: transfer
parts.role: 13/17 T compound on a Ø3 steel pin (B: no sleeve), big gear outside the +x wall
parts.why_separate: turns between motor-u web and transfer-cheek

parts.name: pinion
parts.role: 14 T on the N10 D-shaft (DSHAFT)

parts.name: journal-cap
parts.role: A/F: flat 2.0 plate over the wall tops above the idler tips, rails on the wall tops, 8 tongues in slots 1-4, transfer notch, lug on idler axle 3
parts.why_separate: one flat cap for the 4 journals (F: also crank 4)
parts.print_orient: top face on the bed, no support

parts.name: motor-u
parts.role: A: -x web (lugs on idler axles 1, 2, ledge over the cap, transfer pin's -x end) + the N10 U along x (open +z) + ear 2 for the holder screw
parts.why_separate: carries the motor and the transfer's -x end; flat yz profile
parts.print_orient: -x face on the bed, U rises along +x, no support

parts.name: transfer-cheek
parts.role: A: +x cheek for the transfer pin + strap over the N10 U, 1 M3x10 into the -y ear
parts.why_separate: closes the U after the motor goes in
parts.print_orient: +x face on the bed, strap rises along -x, no support

parts.name: cell-holder
parts.role: 2S3P AG13 holder; F: no tongue over crank 4, post on the cap top, tab M3 into motor-u ear 2

parts.name: cell-lid
parts.role: snap lid (unchanged)

parts.name: n10-motor
parts.role: N10 3 V gear motor (to buy; not measured)

parts.name: m3-screws
parts.role: ISO 4762 M3 self-tapping into Ø2.5 pilots: 2 x M3x6 (keel), 2 x M3x10 (strap 1, holder 1); ISO 7380 button head (Ø5.7 x 1.65, 2 mm hex key): 3 x M3x10 (idler axles 1-3) and 1 x M3x16 (transfer axle, listed as transfer-pin)

parts.name: transfer-pin
parts.role: M3 x 16 button head (ISO 7380, Morante 2026-11-27), the transfer's axle (screw, not a dowel); head on the motor-u web's -x face, thread in the web's Ø2.5 pilot, STEEL through the boss and the transfer; entered from -x

parts.name: ag13-cells
parts.role: 6 x AG13, springs and nickel strip

parts.name: ss12d00-switch
parts.role: slide switch

parts.name: leds
parts.role: 2 x 5 mm LED + resistors

parts.name: jst-xh
parts.role: 3-pin JST-XH pair

held.+z: 2 M3x6 heads in the base bosses

joints.name: crank-in-spine
joints.apart_by: lift the cap, lift each crank

held.+z: idler-3 M3x10 button head on lug 3; motor-u ledge

held.-x: M3x16 thread in its Ø2.5 pilot or its head

held.+x: gearbox face on the U end stop

held.-z: post on the cap top, tab on ear 2

alternatives.topic: drive: transfer vs Direct 1 (comparison, probe p3plan/n1var.py, 24 poses)
options: Direct 1: 10 T on idler 1 at 110°, face-mounted N10
alternatives.why: Direct 1 needs a ≥2.0 face plate + GEAR_AXIAL 0.8 between pinion and gearbox, pushing the N10 to x 4.9..25.9: N10↔body −0.79, plate↔body −0.50, N10↔leg-1 −0.12 (overlaps); A keeps the phase-2 envelope (cap↔transfer 0.24, a notch size)

options: A: 25 parts, 8 M3 (2 lengths) + 1 pin, 24 steps
Direct 1: 23 parts, 9 M3 + 2 M1.6 face screws (3 kinds), 22 steps
alternatives.why: Direct 1 saves 2 parts and 2 steps but adds a screw kind on an unmeasured face

options: A: drive 0 mm² (3 flat parts) vs 524 + 151 + sleeves now
alternatives.why: equal; cranks 137 mm² each remain in both

options: A: transfer centre distances through 3 screwed parts (STEEL 0.15 a side vs 0.27 before binding)
Direct 1: N10 face holes/spacing and shaft length assumed (2 x M1.6 at 9 mm, shaft ≥ 6.5 from the face), not bought, N1 fails by 0.8
alternatives.why: A's risk is a coupon; Direct 1's is a body change, which is frozen

alternatives.choice: M3 shanks for the idlers and an M3x16 for the transfer
alternatives.why: fits.STEEL is measured for screw shanks as axles; each idler screw also holds the cap or the motor-u, threaded only in the -x wall so the walls are not squeezed; transfer span 18.7 needs 16 mm: M3x16, nothing to buy (Morante 2026-11-26: «Ok», 3 screw lengths)
Morante's A; one part closes the U and caps the transfer pin
Morante's F: the holder comes out without freeing crank 4

acceptance.text: the parts are imported from cad/legs, cad/eyes, cad/base, cad/body; scale, crank and leg path from cad/motion.py, never copied
the parametric parts may be reshaped where the inside needs it (surfaces moved, stretched or opened), as long as the robot's look passes the judge

every part, screw and contact is in the code that counts the fit; a fit that leaves something out is reported as partial. Wires take no volume (flexible, routed by hand); only a hole or slot where a wire must pass a wall between its two ends (Morante, 2026-11-21: «no consideres los cables ni el espacio que ocupan… si hay que conectar cables entre dos puntos que separa una pared, sí tienes que dejar un agujero o ranura para que pasen»)
assembly order and each part's path checked before the scale
the motor's fit is a separate, screwed part (the motor is bought later and measured; a fix reprints grams)
Morante can change the cells; the switch is reached from outside
two 5 mm LED bores in the eyes, wired by Morante (no eyes board)
the views command renders the robot and jenscolt's assembled meshes in the same views and framing, written as images/reference.png next to the photos
fasteners: M3 everywhere (holes fits.STEEL on Ø3.3), or snap fits (datasheet robot «Phase 1 result», Morante 2026-11-26)
margins, walls and clearances: the standard values of cad/fits.py; changed only where they cause a problem, and put to Morante
print support as little as possible; up to 20-30 % on a part is accepted when a valid solution needs it
screwdriver access: where it blocks a solution, it is put to Morante before the solution is dropped

when something collides: first layout; then the colliding part is reshaped locally to make room (a pocket, relief, notch or bulge), any bulge outward on the shell (base) or the body first; a larger S is not wanted and is only put to Morante when nothing else works (Morante, 2026-11-21: «cada vez que te encuentres con un problema de colisiones, modifica o deforma la pieza local para dar cabida a lo que falta… empiezas por fuera en la carcasa o en el cuerpo»; «no quiero aumentar la escala más»)

views.py places jenscolt's meshes (body, base, eyes, sensor, 8 legs; leg placement as the archived tools/assemble_jenscolt.py) at the robot's S and frame, writes out/reference.stl, and renders robot and reference with tools/mesh_ref.py views; `views.py --reference` writes images/reference.png; meshes are read only here, never by build.py or a gate
cell contacts: conical springs + nickel strip (to buy)
eye LEDs: red or yellow from the Arduino kit, with their resistors placed and counted
wiring through one 3-pin JST-XH (to buy); hook-up wire from the Arduino kit
body held at the front by snap fits (the front screws are boxed in by the eye block and the legs); screws only where they have driver access (Morante, 2026-11-21: «Ok»)
cranks 2 and 3 (and their mirror) 2.6 mm further apart along Y than motion.py's uniform DY, standard fits.LEG_PATH on every leg pair (no waiver); the middle…

B: no printed sleeves; idlers on M3 shanks, transfer on a Ø3 pin
